title: How Much Does One Chat With AI Cost? DeepSeek Gray-Scale Test Shows Consumption Quota and Puts the Bill in Front of You

content_html:
Free AI chat burns money with every message behind the scenes—DeepSeek has decided to lay the books open. Starting November 26, some users report that its web and app are running a limited gray-scale test of a “show usage consumed this turn” feature: after completing a round of conversation, a details page pops up showing the number of tokens consumed in the interaction and the estimated amount, with pricing on par with the API. Personal conversations remain free, but the compute cost of a single conversation is now visible.

A tiny bill, split into three parts

Judging from user screenshots, usage is estimated at “off-peak” pricing, and billing is broken into three dimensions: for the input cache-hit portion, the unit price is 0.02 yuan per million tokens, usage this round was about 185,000, equivalent to 0.0037 yuan; for the cache-miss portion, the unit price is 1 yuan per million tokens, usage was about 12,000, equivalent to 0.012 yuan; for the output portion, the unit price is 4 yuan per million tokens, usage was 1,470, equivalent to 0.0058 yuan. Together, the three add up to no more than two cents, and the difference lies in the structure—so-called cache hits mean the model directly reuses previously computed context K-V cache to avoid recomputation, with a unit price only one-fiftieth that of a miss. In multi-turn conversations, the system caches historical context, and subsequent input is billed at full price only for the “newly added” part, greatly reducing the cumulative cost of long conversations.

A handy reminder: the context is almost used up

At the bottom of the details page, a progress hint has also been added: “As of this round, context usage is…”. When the usage ratio approaches 100%, the system usually warns or automatically truncates earlier conversation to prevent exceeding the model’s maximum context window. First implementing limits, then showing the bill—DeepSeek’s one-two combo makes the cost of “free” perceptible for the first time.
